text:
hana: heads-up, hosted-usw2 GPU pool alerts just spiked — several p95 queueing alarms fired.
leo: seeing it too, p95 latency jumped to ~1.2s and queue length up ~4x vs baseline.
ops-bot: ALERT: gpu_pool_utilization_usw2 > 85% for 3m (fired)
marcus: any recent deploys or big customer jobs? I don’t see automatic scale events.
jen: not from infra deploys. Customer telemetry shows a few heavy realtime retrieval jobs from acct:fastsearch-io around 13:02 UTC.
leo: looks like a burst of short but hot requests — lots of small-context generations causing KV cache churn + high per-token cost.
hana: dashboard link: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/usw2/gpu-pools — check Admission Control > inflight and queued by model.
marcus: I can patch temporary admission threshold to be more strict (lower concurrency) for hosted tier to reduce queue pressure. Tradeoff: more client 429s.
jen: prefer routing-first: divert non-prod traffic to euw1 if possible? Can we auto-route during pressure window?
leo: smart-routing is possible but there’s cross-region latency concerns. For now, short-term mitigation plan:
- throttle incoming hosted API for bursty keys (>X RPS)
- enable small-model fallback for large prompts (route to quantized variant)
- refill pool by spinning up 2 extra nodes (if capacity available)
sre-oncall: I can trigger the node refill; confirming quota and scheduler headroom now.
hana: can you also mute noisy alert on p95 so we stop paging while we triage? keep the higher-sev still active.
marcus: making a quick admission-control patch in k8s HPA policy, will push shortly:
```
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
spec:
  maxReplicas: 48 # bumped from 40 temporarily
  metrics:
  - type: Resource
    resource:
      name: gpu_utilization
      target:
        averageUtilization: 70
```
leo: pushed a canary change to admission service to enforce per-key burst window of 10s — should reduce the short-term spikes.
ops-bot: NOTE: Scheduled scale operation started (operation-id: op-7821) — 2 nodes added
jen: after the canary, queue length dropped ~30% in 90s. p95 dropping too. Great.
hana: cost note: spinning nodes will increase hourly costs; mark this as emergency only and we’ll reconcile with finance after.
marcus: filing a follow-up to analyze root cause and customer pattern (likely onboarding job with poor batching). Will include prompts and model variants.
sre-oncall: leaving the refill running for 20m, will scale down if pressure subsides. Closing alert once metrics stable.
hana: ok thanks everyone — please add any findings to the incident board and tag #customer-success if we need to contact fastsearch-io about better batching. :thumbsup:
